title: Alert Endpoints and Webhook Configuration API
content:
# Alert Endpoints and Webhook Configuration API

## Webhook Configuration

### Create Webhook
```
POST /webhooks
```
Request body:
```json
{
  "name": "Production Alerts",
  "url": "https://your-server.com/clouddash-webhook",
  "events": ["alert.fired", "alert.resolved", "alert.acknowledged"],
  "headers": {
    "Authorization": "Bearer your-token"
  },
  "active": true
}
```

### List Webhooks
```
GET /webhooks
```

### Update Webhook
```
PUT /webhooks/{webhook_id}
```

### Delete Webhook
```
DELETE /webhooks/{webhook_id}
```

### Test Webhook
```
POST /webhooks/{webhook_id}/test
```
Sends a test payload to verify connectivity.

## Webhook Events

| Event | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| alert.fired | An alert threshold was breached |
| alert.resolved | An alert returned to normal |
| alert.acknowledged | An alert was acknowledged by a user |
| incident.created | A new incident was created |
| incident.resolved | An incident was resolved |
| integration.disconnected | A cloud integration lost connectivity |

## Webhook Payload Format

All webhook payloads follow this structure:
```json
{
  "id": "evt_abc123",
  "event_type": "alert.fired",
  "timestamp": "2026-04-15T10:30:00Z",
  "data": {
    "alert_id": "alert-456",
    "alert_name": "High CPU Usage",
    "severity": "critical",
    "resource": "i-0abc123def456",
    "metric": "aws.ec2.cpu_utilization",
    "value": 95.2,
    "threshold": 90,
    "dashboard_url": "https://app.clouddash.io/alerts/alert-456"
  }
}
```

## Webhook Security

- All webhook payloads include an `X-CloudDash-Signature` header.
- The signature is an HMAC-SHA256 hash of the payload body using your webhook signing secret.
- Verify the signature on your server to ensure the request is from CloudDash.
- Signing secret is available under **Settings > Integrations > Webhooks > Signing Secret**.
